item.text:
**What changed.** Three redirect helpers moved from `httpx/_utils.py` to `httpx/_client.py` and gained leading underscores. Their logic is identical. Five existing tests moved from `tests/test_utils.py` to `tests/client/test_headers.py` without changing their assertions. [Client helpers](httpx/_client.py:61) · [Redirect header tests](tests/client/test_headers.py:240)

**Bugs and risks.** I found no runtime regression in the diff. External code that imports the old private helper names from `httpx._utils` or `httpx._client` will break. The moved `Host` tests also have a pre-existing blind spot. The original and expected `Host` values are identical after URL normalization, so the tests can pass even if the cross-origin rewrite is skipped. [Redirect header tests](tests/client/test_headers.py:240)

**Affected callers and behavior.** `BaseClient._build_redirect_request` calls `_redirect_headers` for both `Client` and `AsyncClient`, whether they follow the redirect or expose it as `response.next_request`. The same path serves the top-level request helpers and CLI through `Client`. Cross-origin redirects still rewrite `Host` and strip `Authorization`, with the existing exception for same-host HTTP:80 → HTTPS:443 upgrades. I found no other in-repo users of the moved helpers. [Shared redirect builder](httpx/_client.py:474) · [Header handling](httpx/_client.py:545) · [Sync](httpx/_client.py:976) · [Async](httpx/_client.py:1679) · [API](httpx/_api.py:102) · [CLI](httpx/_main.py:491)

`git diff --check` passed. I did not run the tests.
